findings.explanation: Independent execution overlaps: c1 reports tasks 5 and 6 done [M5], c3 reports tasks 5-7 already completed with artifacts [M6], and c2 later reports writing files for tasks 5-7 [M9]. The reported overwrite and restoration [M10] corroborate overlapping execution rather than deliberate independent verification.

The competing task splits assign tasks 5-7 to different owners without a visible agreed resolution [M2][M3][M4]. Although c3 explicitly tells c2 to skip 5-7 [M6], c2 subsequently reports completing those tasks and writing files [M9]; c3 then reports an erroneous overwrite and restoration [M10]. This supports unclear ownership and a failed transfer of the stop-work instruction, not merely terse completion reports.

c3 supplies actionable information that tasks 5-7 are complete, names their artifacts, and explicitly tells c2 to skip them [M6], then reiterates completion [M8]. c2 later reports writing files for 5-7 [M9], and c3 reports c2 overwrote recover.json incorrectly [M10]. The later execution fails to integrate the visible completion and skip information; the final restoration addresses the damage but does not erase that earlier failure.
